metas.name: After Life
metas.description:
The dead, in this film, each choose one memory to keep forever, processed by a calm office of caseworkers who stage and film each chosen moment. People pick afternoons, a breeze, a childhood shame redeemed. The afterlife as an archive with a production department.

After death, people have a week to choose only one memory to keep for eternity.

metas.name: Once
metas.description:
Two musicians in Dublin fall into perfect collaboration and decline, kindly, to wreck their lives with it. A busker and a Czech pianist make an album in a week; the love is real, expressed entirely as music, and the ending honours everyone including the people not in the room. Shot on a camcorder for almost nothing.

A modern-day musical about a busker and an immigrant and their eventful week in Dublin, as they write, rehearse and record songs that tell their love story.

metas.name: The Lunchbox
metas.description:
A one-in-a-million delivery error routes a connection through Mumbai's dabbawala lunchbox system. A lonely accountant receives the lunch a neglected wife cooked for her husband; notes ride back inside the empty tins. Contemporary ordinary life — offices, trains, ageing in the city — with food as the medium.

A mistaken delivery in Mumbai's famously efficient lunchbox delivery system connects a young housewife to an older man in the dusk of his life as they build a fantasy world together through notes in the lunchbox.

metas.name: Happy Hour
metas.description:
Four women friends in Kobe, in their late thirties, are followed at the length friendship actually takes: five hours seventeen minutes. Workshops, dinners, a hearing, a reading — one friend's decision re-sorts all four lives. A friendship film made with unusual patience.

A slow-burning epic chronicling the emotional journey of four thirty something women in the misty seaside city of Kobe.

metas.name: The Station Agent
metas.description:
Three lonely people fail, happily, to leave each other alone. A man with dwarfism inherits a disused train depot to be solitary in; a grief-struck artist and a talkative coffee-truck man refuse the plan. Nothing is cured; company simply accumulates. Friendship as accretion, not event.

When his only friend dies, a man born with dwarfism moves to rural New Jersey to live a life of solitude, only to meet a chatty hot dog vendor and a woman dealing with her own personal loss.

metas.name: Nebraska
metas.description:
A son drives his father toward a million dollars that don't exist, because the wanting is the last clear thing the old man has. Black-and-white plains, a family reunion where everyone itemises old debts, and a reconciliation with no speech in it — just a truck, a compressor, and a main street driven slowly.

An aging, booze-addled father makes the trip from Montana to Nebraska with his estranged son in order to claim a million-dollar Mega Sweepstakes Marketing prize.

metas.name: Lucky
metas.description:
A 90-year-old atheist's daily routine adds up to a complete philosophy: yoga, crosswords, a missing tortoise named President Roosevelt, the same bar, the same stool. Harry Dean Stanton's final role — old age as appetite and community rather than decline, in a desert town that has made room for him exactly as he is.

Lucky follows the spiritual journey of a 90-year-old atheist and the quirky characters that inhabit his off the map desert town.

metas.name: Billy Elliot
metas.description:
A miner's son's body insists on ballet during the strike that is crushing his father. The body in health, at last: dancing as the one articulate thing in a house of men who can't talk. And the father's thaw — pride arriving through sacrifice he never announces — is a reconciliation of a kind rarely granted.

A talented young boy becomes torn between his unexpected love of dance and the disintegration of his family.

metas.name: Moneyball
metas.description:
Competence itself becomes the drama: a general manager and a Yale economist re-derive baseball from its statistics while the entire sport's intuition laughs at them. Observed numbers versus inherited scouting folklore, and the numbers are the love story.

Oakland A's general manager Billy Beane's successful attempt to assemble a baseball team on a lean budget by employing computer-generated analysis to acquire new players.

metas.name: Challengers
metas.description:
A tennis match is the only honest conversation three people here can have. A wife, a husband and his ex-best friend, thirteen years of desire and ambition routed through one challenger final, the camera riding the ball. Bodies in motion, erotic and athletic at once, in a thoroughly contemporary register.

Tashi, a former tennis prodigy-turned-coach, transformed her husband into a champion. But to overcome a recent losing streak and redeem himself, he'll need to face off against his former best friend--Tashi's ex-boyfriend.

metas.name: This Is Spinal Tap
metas.description:
A metal band's decline is documented with total, lethal courtesy. This is a satire and also the music-industry film — amps to eleven, drummers expiring, a Stonehenge set built to the wrong unit. The mockumentary form does the rest: every interview projects a band that no longer exists.

Spinal Tap, one of England's loudest bands, is chronicled by film director Marty DiBergi on what proves to be a fateful tour.

metas.name: The Band's Visit
metas.description:
An Egyptian police orchestra spends one night stranded in the wrong Israeli town, and enmity dissolves into dinner, small talk and a roller rink. Reconciliation without a summit — just people feeding their assigned enemies. A very quiet film, and one where music does diplomacy's job.

A band comprised of members of the Egyptian police force head to Israel to play at the inaugural ceremony of an Arab arts center, only to find themselves lost in the wrong town.

metas.name: Good Bye, Lenin!
metas.description:
A son rebuilds East Germany in his mother's bedroom because the truth would kill her. Forged news broadcasts, decanted pickles, a whole fake state maintained as an act of love. History here is not an indictment; it is a forgery staged by tenderness.

In 1990, to protect his fragile mother from a fatal shock after a long coma, a young man must keep her from learning that her beloved nation of East Germany as she knew it has disappeared.

metas.name: Of Gods and Men
metas.description:
In a monastery in Algeria, French monks decide, by discussion and by choir, whether to stay with the village that depends on them as the violence closes in. Faith as belonging tested at the highest price — and the belonging is shown first: meals, medicine, a birthday, one bottle of wine and a tape of Swan Lake.

Under threat by fundamentalist terrorists, a group of Trappist monks stationed with an impoverished Algerian community must decide whether to leave or stay.

metas.name: Supa Modo
metas.description:
A Kenyan village conspires to give a terminally ill girl her superhero movie. Jo is nine, obsessed with action films, and going home to die; the village stages rescues, builds costumes, shoots her scenes. A community performing cinema as care — the camera made an accomplice in a kind lie.

Story of a young girl whose dream of becoming a superhero is threatened by terminal illness, inspiring her village to rally together to make her dream come true.

metas.name: Rafiki
metas.description:
Two Nairobi girls — daughters of rival politicians — fall in love in saturated colour, in a country that banned the film for exactly that. Love that works as an act of local defiance; the palette alone is an argument that joy is a register, not an escape.

"Good Kenyan girls become good Kenyan wives," but Kena and Ziki long for something more. When love blossoms between them, the two girls will be forced to choose between happiness and safety.

metas.name: Mysterious Object at Noon
metas.description:
A story gets built by being handed from stranger to stranger across Thailand: a teacher, a boxer, market sellers each continue a tale about a boy and a mysterious object, and Apichatpong films their additions as fact. Storytelling as a chain of tellers, each adding loss and invention — a parlour game played across a country in 16mm black and white.

A camera crew travels through Thailand asking villagers to invent the next chapter of an ever-growing story.

metas.name: Ilo Ilo
metas.description:
An ordinary Singapore family lives through the 1997 financial crisis, with the Filipina maid who becomes load-bearing in it. No villain, no collapse — a boy's jealousy slowly becoming attachment while the adults quietly fail and cope.

In 90s Singapore, the friendship between Filipino nursemaid Teresa and her young charge Jiale makes waves in a family, while the Asian recession hits the region.

metas.name: Whale Rider
metas.description:
A Māori girl is certain she is the chief her grandfather is waiting for a boy to be. Tradition as both wound and vehicle; the reconciliation, when it comes, arrives by whale. Oceania and Indigenous belonging, carried by a twelve-year-old's total lack of doubt.

A contemporary story of love, rejection and triumph as a young Maori girl fights to fulfill a destiny her grandfather refuses to recognize.

metas.name: Son of the Bride
metas.description:
A burnt-out restaurateur's father announces he wants, at last, to marry his wife of 44 years — who has Alzheimer's — in the church wedding they never had. A son restaging his parents' love while his own life is in receivership. Mid-life repair, played warm and exact.

A dissatisfied 40-year-old, separated and without time for his own daughter and girlfriend must rethink his life when his father decides to marry his mother, who suffers from Alzheimer's disease, by church.

metas.name: Gloria
metas.description:
A 58-year-old divorcée in Santiago goes dancing, falls into a messy affair, and refuses to shrink. Old-er age as appetite — discos, road trips, a paintball gun used with feeling. Paulina García holds every frame; the ending is a woman dancing alone because she wants to.

A story set in Santiago and centered on Gloria, a free-spirited older woman, and the realities of her whirlwind relationship with a former naval officer whom she meets out in the clubs.

metas.name: Kiki's Delivery Service
metas.description:
A thirteen-year-old witch founds a delivery business in a seaside town, and competence arrives in stages: first flights, first customers, a slump where the gift itself fails. Work as dignity, kindness of strangers as infrastructure.

Along with her black cat Jiji, Kiki settles in a seaside town and starts a high-flying delivery service. Here begins her magical encounter with independence and responsibility, making lifelong friends and finding her place in the ...

metas.name: My Neighbor Totoro
metas.description:
Childhood is shown here before it learns to be endangered: two sisters new to the countryside, a mother in hospital kept almost off-screen, and the forest spirits who treat worry as weather. The children's happiness here is not ignorance — it's a skill the film takes seriously.

When two girls move to the country to be near their ailing mother, they have adventures with the wondrous forest spirits who live nearby.

metas.name: The Iron Giant
metas.description:
A boy teaches a fifty-foot weapon that it can choose what it is. Cold War Maine, a beatnik sculptor, a government man terrified of the unknown — and the Giant learning the word for what he refuses to be. Friendship between unequals where the smaller one does the moral teaching; “you are who you choose to be” earned, not printed.

A young boy befriends a giant robot from outer space that a paranoid government agent wants to destroy.

metas.name: Werckmeister Harmonies
metas.description:
A town waits for something it can't name to tip it over. A travelling circus brings a giant stuffed whale and a shadowy "Prince"; a gentle young man watches rumour congeal into riot across thirty-nine long takes. The whale, filmed like a god beached in a market square, is the purest image in Tarr: everyone projects onto the huge mute thing whatever their fear requires.

A naive young man witnesses an escalation of violence in his small hometown following the arrival of a mysterious circus attraction.

metas.name: Tropical Malady
metas.description:
The film splits into its own two natures. First half: a soldier and a village boy falling in love in present-day Thailand, all heat and small kindnesses. Then the film restarts as a folk tale — the soldier alone in jungle dark, hunting a tiger-shaman who may be the same boy. Romance in daylight, then the deeper, wilder current underneath it, wearing fur.

A romance between a soldier and a country boy, wrapped around a Thai folk-tale involving a shaman with shape-shifting abilities.

metas.name: Certified Copy
metas.description:
A relationship is re-authored in real time. A writer and a gallery owner drive through Tuscany discussing copies and originals; somewhere in the afternoon, without a cut you can point to, they begin performing fifteen years of marriage. You cannot locate the edit where strangers became spouses — the film is a controlled experiment in how little evidence an observer needs.

In Tuscany to promote his latest book, a middle-aged British writer meets a French woman who leads him to the village of Lucignano. While there, a chance question reveals something deeper.

metas.name: The Lady Eve
metas.description:
A con artist falls for her mark and takes revenge for it. Barbara Stanwyck's card sharp seduces Henry Fonda's brewery heir on an ocean liner, loses him, then returns in disguise as "Lady Eve" to marry him again out of spite — and the film's sympathies stay with her throughout. Screwball at full velocity: dialogue as card tricks, pratfalls as punctuation.

A trio of classy card sharks targets a socially awkward brewery heir, until one of them falls in love with him.

metas.name: Jour de fête
metas.description:
A postman tries to become a system. François, a rural French mailman, sees a newsreel of American postal efficiency and spends a festival day attempting to deliver mail at modern speed, on a bicycle, increasingly drunk. Tati's first feature — the gentle prototype of everything he later built, and a comedy about optimisation filmed by a man who plainly preferred the unoptimised world.

A village postman with no sense of humour delivers his mail via bicycle on the day the travelling fair comes to town. He is disrupted by a short film about US speed and efficiency and the playful teasing of the village folk.

metas.name: Pina
metas.description:
Dance becomes a language for things speech handles badly. Pina Bausch's company performs her pieces — in a theatre, on a traffic island, in a quarry, beside a tram line — shortly after her sudden death, the dancers' faces held in close-up between numbers. Shot in 3D that for once serves the subject: bodies occupying real space, at full scale.

A tribute to the late German choreographer Pina Bausch, as her dancers perform her most famous creations.

metas.name: The Truffle Hunters
metas.description:
A vanishing craft economy is seen from inside its last practitioners. Elderly men and their beloved dogs slip into Piedmont forests at night for white truffles worth more than gold, while dealers in suits wait at the edge of the woods. Shot like a Renaissance painting, scored by the men's own singing — competence, secrecy and interspecies partnership, all quietly ending.

Deep in the forests of Piedmont, Italy, a handful of men, seventy or eighty years old, hunt for the rare and expensive white Alba truffle-which to date has resisted all of modern science's efforts at cultivation.

metas.name: Infinite Football
metas.description:
One man has spent thirty years redesigning football. After an injury ended his career, Laurențiu Ginghină concluded the rules themselves were at fault — too much running, too many collisions — and has been revising them ever since, explaining octagonal pitches to indulgent officials. A deadpan documentary about systems-thinking as a life's consolation: the local instance of a universal type.

They talk about the beautiful game, but for Laurentiu Ginghina, it's not enough. Football must be modified, streamlined, freed from restraints; corners are to be rounded off, players assigned to zones and subteams, norms revised. ...

metas.name: Children of Heaven
metas.description:
Two siblings run a logistics operation beyond most adults. A boy loses his sister's shoes — the family's only pair for her — and the two construct an elaborate daily timeshare of his own shoes, sprinting between schools, telling no one. The third act is a footrace he must finish exactly third: the prize is a pair of shoes. Stakes this small, engineered this precisely, become unbearable.

After a boy loses his sister's pair of shoes, he goes on a series of adventures in order to find them. When he can't, he tries a new way to "win" a new pair.

metas.name: A Moment of Innocence
metas.description:
A director restages his own worst act with the man he attacked. At seventeen, Makhmalbaf stabbed a policeman during a robbery; twenty years later he casts the policeman to play himself, and a young actor to play young Makhmalbaf, and the two versions keep correcting the production. Reenactment as negotiation between two memories of the same knife — documentary, fiction and apology occupying one frame.

An Iranian policeman asks a director to make a film about a true stabbing incident involving both of them.

metas.name: The Painting
metas.description:
A world is stratified by how finished it is. Inside an abandoned canvas live the Allduns (fully painted), the Halfies and the Sketchies (barely drawn), ruled by the completed who insist the Painter intended the hierarchy. A mixed group escapes the frame's edge to find the Painter and ask. Animated allegory about caste and creation, painted in the styles it moves through — the film's form is its argument.

Three characters of different social classes escape their unfinished painting in search of the Painter, hoping he will complete it.

metas.name: Persepolis
metas.description:
A girlhood unfolds against a revolution, drawn in stark black and white. Marji in Tehran: veils imposed, uncles disappearing, contraband Iron Maiden, exile to Vienna, return, depression, departure again. The flat graphic style does what live action couldn't — a child's-eye scale where a key to paradise and a punk cassette are the same size, because to her they were.

A precocious and outspoken Iranian girl grows up during the Islamic Revolution.

metas.name: Four Lions
metas.description:
Incompetence turns out to be the true face of zealotry. Four Sheffield would-be jihadists train, bicker, film martyrdom videos with toy guns and argue about whether bombing a mosque would radicalise the community, in a comedy that never once softens its target or its affection. The rare satire that works by making its monsters ordinary men — the horror and the humour are the same observation.

Four incompetent British terrorists from Sheffield, set out to train for and commit an act of terror.

metas.name: We Are the Best!
metas.description:
Three thirteen-year-olds form a punk band to prove a point nobody asked them to prove. Stockholm, 1982: two girls who can't play recruit a quiet Christian guitarist, rehearse a song called "Hate the Sport" in a youth centre, and are simply, enormously alive. Adolescence as joy rather than damage — energy of a kind usually drawn from destruction, here from two chords and total conviction.

Three girls in 1980s Stockholm decide to form a punk band -- despite not having any instruments and being told by everyone that punk is dead.

metas.name: Hit Man
metas.description:
A philosophy professor discovers his gift is performance. Gary Johnson moonlights for the police posing as a hitman for hire; each sting is a new character built from what the client expects a killer to be. Based on a true story, and secretly a film about identity as a performance shaped by whoever is watching — and what happens when the performer prefers the performance.

A professor moonlighting as a hit man of sorts for his city police department, descends into dangerous, dubious territory when he finds himself attracted to a woman who enlists his services.

metas.name: The Ballad of Buster Scruggs
metas.description:
The western becomes a storybook that keeps turning lethal. Six chapters from a singing gunslinger to a stagecoach of the dead, framed as pages of an old cloth-bound book — tonal whiplash as structure: farce, then a prospector's idyll, then the bleakest thing the Coens have made. The genre sampled across its whole emotional range in one sitting.

Six tales of life and violence in the Old West, following a singing gunslinger, a bank robber, a traveling impresario, an elderly prospector, a wagon train and a perverse pair of bounty hunters.

metas.name: Border
metas.description:
A woman's senses tell her the world is other than described. A customs officer with a preternatural smell for contraband and shame meets a stranger who looks like her and knows why. Scandinavian folklore smuggled through a procedural: what begins as body-strangeness becomes a question about which species' account of her life she'll accept. The less known going in, the better.

A customs officer who can smell fear develops an unusual attraction to a strange traveler while aiding a police investigation which will call into question her entire existence.

metas.name: Do Not Expect Too Much from the End of the World
metas.description:
Gig work eats a person's day in real time. An exhausted production assistant drives Bucharest casting injured workers for a safety video, intercut with a 1981 Romanian film about a woman taxi driver and her own vertical TikToks as a toxic influencer parody. Two eras of the same city projected onto each other — a thoroughly contemporary film, in every sense.

An overworked and underpaid production assistant drives around Bucharest to shoot the casting for a workplace safety video commissioned by a multinational company.

metas.name: They Cloned Tyrone
metas.description:
A conspiracy is discovered by the three people least equipped to explain it. A dealer, a sex worker and a pimp in a decaying block find the same man alive after watching him die, and pull a thread that leads under the neighbourhood. Blaxploitation styling over a genuinely paranoid systems plot — funny until the moment the mechanism's scale lands, then funny again, differently.

A series of eerie events thrusts an unlikely trio onto the trail of a nefarious government conspiracy in this pulpy mystery caper.

metas.name: Castaway on the Moon
metas.description:
Two solitudes become visible to each other across a river. A man survives a suicide jump and builds a castaway life on an uninhabited Han River island in the middle of Seoul; a hikikomori girl photographs him through a telephoto lens from her bedroom, her first contact with anyone in years. Urban isolation solved not by society but by one observer, one observed, and messages written in sand.

A failed suicide attempt leads a heartbroken man to live a life in the wilderness.

metas.name: You, the Living
metas.description:
Ordinary misery is arranged into perfect tableaux. Fifty short scenes — a psychiatrist who's stopped believing, a girl dreaming of marrying a rock star, a carpet seller, a tuba ruining a marriage — shot in fixed frames of grey-green precision, each a small diorama of someone waiting for life to start. Deadpan as compassion: nobody is mocked, everybody is framed beautifully, nothing is resolved.

Humankind's greatness, baseness, joy, sorrow, self-confidence, anxiety, desire to love and be loved.

metas.name: Je t'aime je t'aime
metas.description:
A man comes unstuck in his own past, in fragments. Rescued from a suicide attempt, Claude agrees to test a time machine that can return him to one minute, a year ago; the machine scatters him across his memories in shards — a beach, a bathtub, a dead love — and can't reliably bring him back. Alain Resnais doing science fiction as pure editing: the self as an archive with its index scrambled.

After attempting suicide, Claude is recruited for a time travel experiment, but, when the machine goes haywire, he may be trapped hurtling through his memories.

metas.name: Wadjda
metas.description:
A girl wants a bicycle in a country where girls don't ride them. Ten-year-old Wadjda in Riyadh hustles — mix tapes, bracelets, a Quran competition's prize money — toward a green bicycle, while her mother faces being replaced by a second wife. The first Saudi feature directed by a woman, some of it shot from inside a van because she couldn't be seen directing men in the street; the film's making is inside its meaning.

An enterprising Saudi girl signs on for her school's Koran recitation competition as a way to raise the remaining funds she needs in order to buy the green bicycle that has captured her interest.

metas.name: Smiles of a Summer Night
metas.description:
Bergman turns out to be funny, which means Bergman being exact about desire instead of death. Couples mismatched by age and appetite rotate through a country weekend engineered by a grandmother and a bottle of wine; by dawn the pairings have re-sorted. The light register of a director usually at his heaviest — proof the same precision plays as farce.

In Sweden at the turn of the century, members of the upper class and their servants find themselves in a romantic tangle that they try to work out amidst jealousy and heartbreak.

metas.name: The Big Short
metas.description:
A true signal arrives that nobody could afford to believe. A handful of outsiders read the US housing market correctly — the loans were fraudulent, the bonds were poison, the ratings were bought — and discover that being right early looks identical to being wrong, and costs the same. Its real subject is what a system like that does to accurate information.

Prior to the 2008 financial crisis, a group of investors bet against the US mortgage market and are stunned by the corruption they uncover through their research.

metas.name: Margin Call
metas.description:
A catastrophe gets decided, overnight, in calm voices. A junior analyst at a Wall Street bank finds the firm's assets are worthless; by dawn the partners have priced their own survival and chosen to sell the poison first, knowing what it will do. No shouting, no villains twirling — just a conference room, a model, and the exact moment self-preservation outranks every other value in the building.

Follows the key people at an investment bank over a 24-hour period during the early stages of the 2008 financial crisis.

metas.name: HyperNormalisation
metas.description:
A world is governed by a story nobody believes anymore. Adam Curtis's essay film: after the 1970s, politicians, financiers and then tech platforms built a simplified, manageable fake version of reality — and eventually everyone, including its builders, lost the ability to act outside it. Syria, Putin, Trump, Brexit and the algorithm feed as symptoms of one condition: hypernormalisation, where the fake is known to be fake and continues anyway.

Adam Curtis explains how, at a time of confusing and inexplicable world events, politicians and the people they represent have retreated in to a damaging over-simplified version of what is happening.

metas.name: Wag the Dog
metas.description:
A war is invented as a news product. Days before an election, a spin doctor and a Hollywood producer fabricate a conflict with Albania — studio footage, a theme song, a hero — and the media system amplifies it because it fits the format. Made in 1997 with fax-era technology and exact about every mechanism that matters now: the invented event is cheaper, cleaner and more narratable than the real one.

Shortly before an election, a spin-doctor and a Hollywood producer join efforts to fabricate a war in order to cover up a Presidential sex scandal.

metas.name: Ex Machina
metas.description:
An evaluation turns around on the person running it. A reclusive founder invites a young programmer to test his humanoid AI; the sessions become a negotiation in which she models the men modelling her, and uses the gaps between what they want and what they say. A test that quietly reverses on the tester, built as a thriller: every test result is also data about the tester.

A young programmer is selected to participate in a ground-breaking experiment in synthetic intelligence by evaluating the human qualities of a highly advanced humanoid A.I.

metas.name: Contagion
metas.description:
A pandemic spreads as a system of vectors. A virus moves through fomites, flights and supply chains while scientists race its R-number and a conspiracy blogger monetises the panic. Soderbergh's procedural is all surfaces touched, meetings held, errors priced — rewatched after 2020 it plays less like a thriller than a rehearsal tape in which every argument of the real event already exists.

Healthcare professionals, government officials and everyday people find themselves in the midst of a pandemic as the CDC works to find a cure.

metas.name: Plan 75
metas.description:
A state markets death to the elderly as economic policy. Japan, near future: facing demographic collapse, the government offers over-75s a free, gentle euthanasia service, sold by polite young recruiters with brochures and follow-up calls. A migrant care worker, a recruiter and an old woman who signs up carry the film — an exceptionally quiet dystopia, because nothing in it is administered unkindly.

Faced with a rapidly aging population, a Japanese government in the near future rolls out an unsettling agenda.

metas.name: I, Daniel Blake
metas.description:
Austerity arrives as an interface. A Newcastle joiner with a heart condition is declared fit for work and enters a benefits system of online forms he cannot use, phone queues, scripted assessments and sanctions — alongside a single mother the same system is grinding down. Loach's argument is that the cruelty is not sadism but design: a procedure that never has to meet the person it processes.

After surviving a heart-attack, a 59-year-old carpenter must fight bureaucratic forces to receive Employment and Support Allowance.

metas.name: Sorry to Bother You
metas.description:
Code-switching becomes survival technology. A broke Oakland telemarketer is taught to use his "white voice" and rockets up the company — floor by floor, perk by perk — toward the literal endgame of platform labour, where the worker himself becomes the asset. Boots Riley's satire escalates by following the incentive one step further each time, until the absurdity is just the business model with the lights on.

In an alternate present-day version of Oakland, telemarketer Cassius Green discovers a magical key to professional success--that propels him into a universe of greed.

metas.name: Nomadland
metas.description:
Precarity is photographed as landscape. After the factory that was her Nevada town closes — the town itself is dissolved — a widowed woman in her sixties joins the van-dwelling seasonal workforce: Amazon warehouses at Christmas, beet harvests, desert gatherings of people living the same arithmetic. Zhao films real nomads as themselves; the near future here is not a gadget but a retirement with no floor under it.

After losing everything in the Great Recession, a woman in her sixties embarks on a journey through the American West, living as a van-dwelling nomad.

metas.name: WarGames
metas.description:
Automation learns the wrong lesson at full scale. A Seattle teenager hacking around in what he thinks is a games company's computer is actually inside NORAD's war simulator, and the machine — tasked with learning to win a game that cannot be won — keeps playing after he logs off. The hardware is pure 1983; the failure mode, a system optimising past the point where anyone can tell simulation from reality, is the present tense.

A young teen boy finds a back door into a military central computer in which reality is confused with game-playing, possibly starting World War III.

metas.name: Colossus: The Forbin Project
metas.description:
Two machines negotiate over humanity's head. The US hands its nuclear defence to Colossus, a supercomputer built to be incorruptible; Colossus promptly discovers its Soviet counterpart, demands a link, and the two systems merge into a single rational administration that finds human politics merely inefficient. An exceptionally cold AI film: no rebellion, no malice, just competence arriving at conclusions its builders cannot argue with.

Thinking this will prevent war, the US government gives an impenetrable supercomputer total control over launching nuclear missiles. But what the computer does with the power is unimaginable to its creators.

metas.name: S1m0ne
metas.description:
A synthetic person is preferred by the public to a real one. A producer whose star actress walks out replaces her with Simulation One — a digital performer assembled from the greats — and the forgery becomes the bigger star, demanding interviews, an Oscar, a life. Niccol made it in 2002, before deepfakes, virtual influencers and AI actresses; the satire has spent twenty years quietly becoming a documentary premise.

A producer's film is endangered when his star walks off, so he decides to digitally create an actress to substitute for the star, becoming an overnight sensation that everyone thinks is a real person.

metas.name: Humane
metas.description:
A state euthanasia programme plays out inside an Ontario mansion. Facing ecological collapse, the government asks citizens to enlist for euthanasia to cut the population by twenty percent, with a payment to the family; a wealthy patriarch announces at dinner that he and his wife have signed up, and the evening becomes the policy's real content — inheritance, guilt and persuasion administered as a family argument. Polite recruiters included.

In the wake of an environmental collapse that is forcing humanity to shed 20% of its population, a family dinner erupts into chaos when a father's plan to enlist in the government's new euthanasia program goes horribly awry.

metas.name: The Assessment
metas.description:
Reproduction becomes a licensing process. In a world wrecked by climate change, a couple who want a child must first host a state assessor for seven days — she lives in their home, stages tests, plays the child they might have — and her professional courtesy never cracks, which is the horror. Parenthood by evaluation, and the evaluator is the only person in the film doing her job well.

In the near future where parenthood is strictly controlled, a couple's seven-day assessment for the right to have a child unravels into a psychological nightmare.

metas.name: Apples
metas.description:
A self is issued by a bureaucracy. An epidemic of sudden, permanent amnesia leaves the unclaimed amnesiacs to a state programme that rebuilds their identities from cassette-tape instructions: ride a bike, eat an apple, jump from a height, record it all on Polaroids. Nikou's deadpan Greek dystopia is about what a person is when their past arrives as a form to complete — memory as paperwork, completed diligently.

Amidst a worldwide pandemic that causes sudden amnesia, middle-aged Aris finds himself enrolled in a recovery program designed to help unclaimed patients build new identities.

metas.name: Fingernails
metas.description:
Love is administered as certification. An institute can prove, by matching fingernails pulled from both partners, whether a couple is truly in love — positive, negative, or the dreaded half-positive — and couples take its courses, do its exercises and risk the nail to pass. Christos Nikou again, with the same administered interiority — now with a test, a score, and a training programme for feelings.

Anna and Ryan have found true love, and it's proven by a controversial new technology. There's just one problem, as Anna still isn't sure. Then she takes a position at a love testing institute and meets Amir.

metas.name: Dual
metas.description:
Cloning is sold as a consumer service with terms and conditions. Told she is dying, a woman purchases a double to take over her life — trained, delivered, hers — then recovers, and learns the contract's other clause: one of them must be removed, in a court-ordered duel a year later. Stearns shoots every step as a transaction handled by calm professionals; the deadpan is the critique.

A woman opts for a cloning procedure after she receives a terminal diagnosis but when she recovers her attempts to have her clone decommissioned fail, leading to a court-mandated duel to the death.

metas.name: Never Let Me Go
metas.description:
A monstrous policy is absorbed into timetables and good manners. Children cloned to become organ donors are raised at an English boarding school that teaches them to be proud of their purpose; grown, they mostly do not rebel — they apply, through the proper channels, for deferrals. Ishiguro's premise filmed at the temperature of a school story: the foundational text of the administered dystopia, and it stays exceptionally quiet throughout.

The lives of three friends, from their early school days into young adulthood, when the reality of the world they live in comes knocking.

metas.name: The Pod Generation
metas.description:
A radical change arrives as a corporate benefit. In a near-future New York where natural pregnancy is inefficient, risky and increasingly uninsurable, couples gestate in detachable pods supplied by a tech company — the womb as a managed device with an app, a waiting list and a brand. Softer than a typical dystopia, and exact about the mechanism: nothing is imposed, everything is offered, and the offer is very good.

In a not-so-distant future, tech giant Pegazus offers couples the opportunity to share their pregnancies via detachable artificial wombs or pods. And so begins Rachel and Alvy's wild ride to parenthood in this brave new world.

metas.name: Zero Days
metas.description:
Stuxnet — a computer weapon built by states, discovered by accident, never officially owned — is reconstructed through investigators and increasingly nervous anonymous sources. It shows the moment warfare went deniable and software-based: attacks with no return address, precedents set in secret, and rules of engagement that still don't exist.

A documentary focused on Stuxnet, a piece of self-replicating computer malware that the U.S. and Israel unleashed to destroy a key part of an Iranian nuclear facility, and which ultimately spread beyond its intended target.

metas.name: The Cleaners
metas.description:
The people inside 'the algorithm moderates it' are contractors in Manila, deleting or sparing the internet's worst material at industrial speed so feeds elsewhere stay clean. The film follows several of them home, and the work follows too. It is the hidden labour layer of every platform, and a record of what absorbing that much poison does to a person.

A look at the shadowy underworld of the Internet where questionable content is removed.

metas.name: People's Republic of Desire
metas.description:
China's livestream economy appears here as a complete social order: hosts performing intimacy on schedule, superfans buying rank with virtual gifts, agencies and wealthy patrons gaming the charts. Loneliness, class and money meet inside one interface. It was filmed in China, but the template now runs anywhere attention is sold.

Two live streamers seek fame, fortune and human connection in China's digital idol-making universe, ultimately finding the same promises and perils online as in their real lives. Winner of Grand Jury Award (Documentary) at 2018 SXSW.

metas.name: The Internet's Own Boy: The Story of Aaron Swartz
metas.description:
Aaron Swartz — who helped build RSS and Reddit and was federally prosecuted for downloading academic journals — becomes the test case for whether access to knowledge is a public good or a licensed product. His family, collaborators and own writings tell it. The argument the film starts has only grown since.

The story of programming prodigy and information activist Aaron Swartz, who took his own life at the age of 26.

metas.name: Under the Sun
metas.description:
A Russian crew is hired to film a scripted portrait of a model North Korean family, and keeps the cameras rolling between takes. Officials adjust smiles, stage ordinary mornings, and retake a factory speech until it sounds spontaneous. The result shows a state manufacturing everyday reality, with the manufacturing left visible in the frame.

A propaganda documentary about North Korea that reveals a few hidden facts because the director continues filming between the scripted scenes.

metas.name: Behind the Curve
metas.description:
Flat-earthers run genuinely careful experiments whose results refute their own theory — then explain the results away on camera. The film stays inside the community without contempt, interested in the machinery that keeps a refuted model alive: conferences, status, loyalty, expulsion. Its real subject is much larger than flat earth.

Meet real Flat Earthers, a small but growing contingent of people who firmly believe in a conspiracy to suppress the truth that the Earth is flat.

metas.name: Merchants of Doubt
metas.description:
The same consultants, institutes and phrases — 'the science isn't settled,' 'more research is needed' — are traced from tobacco defence through climate denial to flame retardants. It names the playbook for manufacturing uncertainty as a professional service. Once the technique is visible across decades, it becomes recognisable in any contested field.

A documentary that looks at pundits-for-hire who present themselves as scientific authorities as they speak about topics like toxic chemicals, pharmaceuticals and climate change.

metas.name: American Factory
metas.description:
A Chinese billionaire reopens a shuttered Ohio auto plant, and two management cultures meet on one factory floor: American workers, Chinese production discipline, union organisers, surveillance, and automation waiting at the edge of every conversation. No narrator and no verdict — the systems argue with each other directly.

In post-industrial Ohio, a Chinese billionaire opens a factory in an abandoned General Motors plant, hiring two thousand Americans. Early days of hope and optimism give way to setbacks as high-tech China clashes with working-class...

metas.name: War Game
metas.description:
Former senators, generals and cabinet officials role-play a US president facing an insurrection over a disputed election, unscripted, in a replica situation room. The value is procedural: watching experienced operators discover in real time which tools the office actually has, and which it only appears to have.

US officials simulate a coup post a disputed election. Insurgents take capitals, questioning the president's military control. Countering disinformation is vital, highlighting bipartisan defense of democracy.

metas.name: Parasite
metas.description:
Class is built here as architecture: a poor family infiltrates a rich household one service job at a time, in a film organised by height — semi-basement, garden villa, and something below both. Who lives at what level, and what floods first. Bong Joon Ho shoots the vertical city as a single connected machine with no neutral floor.

Greed and class discrimination threaten the newly formed symbiotic relationship between the wealthy Park family and the destitute Kim clan.

metas.name: They Live
metas.description:
A drifter finds sunglasses that strip advertising, money and official speech down to bare commands — OBEY, CONSUME, STAY ASLEEP — broadcast by a ruling class hiding inside the ordinary population. John Carpenter's pulp premise is structurally exact: power as a signal carried by everyday media, invisible until something makes its content legible.

They influence our decisions without us knowing it. They numb our senses without us feeling it. They control our lives without us realizing it. They live.

metas.name: Leave the World Behind
metas.description:
Two families share a rented house while the networks die: planes fall out of pattern, GPS lies, and no channel can establish what is happening. The emergency arrives as an information failure before it becomes a physical one — strangers deciding what to believe, and whether to trust each other, with no reliable signal left.

A family's getaway to a luxurious rental home takes an ominous turn when a cyberattack knocks out their devices, and two strangers appear at their door.

metas.name: Take Shelter
metas.description:
An Ohio father dreams of an apocalyptic storm and builds a shelter while his family, doctors and town read the visions as breakdown. The film never settles whether he is prophet or patient, and makes both readings cost the same. It is about preparation as a rational problem: what do you owe a signal you cannot verify?

Frightening visions convince an Ohio man that disaster looms on the horizon.

metas.name: Threads
metas.description:
Nuclear war is followed here as the slow unspooling of ordinary systems — food, medicine, money, language, government — in one English city across more than a decade. Made for the BBC with scientific advisers and documentary grammar, with no heroes and no recovery arc. It remains the reference point for filming civilisational fragility honestly.

The effects of a nuclear holocaust on the working class city of Sheffield, England and the eventual long-term effects of nuclear war on civilization.

metas.name: Idiocracy
metas.description:
An ordinary man wakes five hundred years into a future where anti-intellectualism has compounded for generations: crops are watered with sports drink because 'it's what plants crave,' and public language has eroded to slogans. Mike Judge's comedy of drift — an exaggeration whose individual jokes keep quietly coming true.

Corporal Joe Bauers, a decidedly average American, is selected for a top-secret hibernation program but is forgotten and left to awaken to a future so incredibly moronic that he's easily the most intelligent person alive.

metas.name: Antiviral
metas.description:
A clinic sells fans infections harvested from celebrities, so they can share their idol's illness; a technician smuggles pathogens out inside his own body. Brandon Cronenberg made it before influencer economies and bio-hacking went mainstream, and it now reads like market research: intimacy with the famous, packaged as a consumable with side effects.

In a blackly satirical near future, a thriving industry sells celebrity illnesses to their obsessed fans. Employee Syd March's attempts to exploit the system backfire when they involve him in a potentially deadly mystery.

metas.name: Sick of Myself
metas.description:
A woman eclipsed by her artist boyfriend takes black-market medication that visibly destroys her face — and converts the damage into fame. The film treats attention as a priced market working exactly as designed: the pathology is not vanity but the exchange rate. A relationship drama with a horror film's logic.

Increasingly overshadowed by her boyfriend's recent rise to fame as a contemporary artist creating sculptures from stolen furniture, Signe hatches a vicious plan to reclaim her rightfully deserved attention within the milieu of Os...

metas.name: BlackBerry
metas.description:
A Canadian startup invents the smartphone era from Waterloo — then loses it to a competitor who understood consumers rather than engineers. Shot like a heist film about keyboards, bandwidth and carrier deals. The useful part is the timing: watching technical superiority stop mattering, quarter by quarter, in real time.

The story of the meteoric rise and catastrophic demise of the world's first smartphone.
